title: Input Normalization and Tokenization Guardrails — Model Serving Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood's standards for input normalization and tokenization compatibility across the inference stack. It prescribes deterministic normalization rules, a tokenization compatibility matrix, regression detection tests, and rollout guidelines for changes that affect user-visible tokenization or input canonicalization. The goal is to avoid subtle output regressions, cost changes, and security inconsistencies that can arise when the pre-processing pipeline, tokenizer, or model variant drift across environments.

Motivation

Tokenization and input normalization are a frequent source of reproducibility and cost issues in production inference: the same logical prompt can map to different token sequences depending on unicode normalization, whitespace handling, or model-specific tokenizers. That produces token-count variability (affecting billing), unpredictable semantic differences, and can break structured prompts and tool-calling. This playbook reduces blast radius by setting deterministic defaults, compatibility requirements, and observable tests.

Scope

- Applies to: Redwood API (hosted), Dedicated and Private runtimes, edge-proxy, ingest-normalizer, runtime-bridge, and client SDKs.
- Not in scope: model training tokenization choices (except insofar as serving must preserve a documented mapping) and third-party adapter behavior outside Redwood's runtime.

Definitions

- Normalization: deterministic conversion of bytes/characters before tokenization (unicode normalization, trailing whitespace, line endings).
- Tokenizer: the byte/wordpiece/merge-based algorithm used by a specific model artifact.
- Tokenization drift: measured difference in token sequences for the same input between two versions of a preprocessor/tokenizer serving a route.

Principles

1. Determinism: normalizer behavior must be deterministic and idempotent; given identical bytes the same canonicalized string is produced.
2. Transparency: every runtime must expose the normalization configuration used for a response in telemetry (normalized_preview field).
3. Minimal exposure: prefer server-side canonicalization to avoid client mistakes; however client SDKs must document and optionally expose the same canonicalization logic for offline reasoning.
4. Low-latency: normalization should add no more than 10ms median added latency in the ingress path for typical short prompts.

Mandatory Normalization Rules (default canonicalizer)

All services must implement the following as the default 'canonicalizer:v1' unless a route explicitly pins a variant: 

- Unicode: apply NFC normalization to all input text.
- Line endings: normalize CR, LF, CRLF to LF.
- Whitespace: collapse sequences of zero-width spaces (U+200B) and normalize consecutive whitespace to single space except inside code-block markers (```).
- Directionality: preserve character directionality but strip explicit bidi controls (U+202A..U+202E).
- Tabs: replace tabs with single space.
- Trailing/leading: trim trailing and leading ASCII whitespace.
- Control characters: drop non-printable control characters except TAB and LF which are normalized above.
- Byte-preserving flag: for routes that require exact binary passthrough (e.g., bytes-based embeddings), canonicalizer must support a passthrough mode that only enforces line ending normalization.

Tokenization Compatibility Matrix

A text table below must be published alongside each model variant and consumed by the route config. Example (displayed as plain text in the model manifest):

| Model family | Tokenizer family | canonicalizer:v1 compatible | notes |
|--------------|------------------|----------------------------:|-------|
| redwood-7B   | bpe-v2           | true                       | uses unicode NFC in training |
| open-ggml-13B| byte-level       | false                      | requires preserving raw bytes for historical artifacts |

Service Requirements

- Edge-proxy: perform canonicalizer:v1 by default. Add header X-Redwood-Normalized-Preview (first 256 chars) and X-Redwood-Token-Preview (first 64 tokens as hex hash) to responses for internal customers.
- Ingest-normalizer: central library (go/text/canonicalizer) used by all Go services; Python runtimes must vendor a behaviorally-equivalent implementation and include a CI compatibility test.
- Runtime-bridge (gRPC frontend to serving): must accept pre-tokenized payloads and verify token counts against server-side tokenizer for billing; mismatches trigger a 409 with detailed diagnostic in internal-only responses.

Change and Migration Process (when updating canonicalizer or tokenizer mapping)

1. Prepare a compatibility test matrix and run across a standardized prompt corpus (prompt-set-serving-normalization) that includes: short prompts, code blocks, whitespace-heavy inputs, emoji, non-latin scripts, and boundary-case unicode.
2. Measure: token-count delta distribution, semantic fuzz-rate (see regression tests below), and cost delta impact (projected monthly cost change at 95th percentile load).
3. If token-count delta > 0.5% for top-tier customers' routes or median added latency > 10ms, the change requires staged canary rollout and an ADR signoff.
4. Canary: deploy to 1% of traffic with traffic shadowing enabled for the remainder; collect telemetry for 72 hours or 5M requests (whichever comes first).
5. If regressions exceed thresholds, abort and roll back. Document outcome and artifact in an ADR linked from the model manifest.

Regression Detection and Tests

- Tokenization drift test (unit): deterministic check comparing token sequences before/after change for a curated set of 5k prompts. Allowed failure rate: 0.1% without ADR.
- Semantic fuzz test (eval): random perturbations of whitespace/punctuation should not change top-1 intent classification for 99.5% of prompts in the intent-suite.
- Billing delta monitor (SLO): monthly token-count change for a model-route baseline must remain within +/-2% or trigger cost review.

Observability and Telemetry

Every inference response (internal telemetry) must include the following metadata fields: 

- normalization_version: e.g., canonicalizer:v1
- tokenizer_id: e.g., redwood-bpe-v2-2026-01
- normalized_preview: first 256 characters after normalization (internal only)
- token_count: integer used for billing computation
- tokenization_hash: SHA256 of token sequence (for drift detection)

Alerting

- Alert: tokenization-drift-high when >0.5% of requests over a rolling 1h window have tokenization_hash mismatches against the golden service. Pager: oncall-runtime.
- Alert: normalization-latency when p99 added latency > 50ms for canonicalizer operation on edge-proxy. Pager: eng-infra.

SDK and Client Guidance

- SDKs must expose a helper normalize_input(text) that uses the same canonicalization rules and produce an RFC describing equivalence with server canonicalizer.
- Clients may submit pre-tokenized payloads; when they do, they must set pretokenized=true and include tokenizer_id. The runtime will verify token counts and fail if inconsistent.

Security and Prompt Injection Considerations

Normalization can be used adversarially to hide injection patterns (e.g., manipulative unicode combining marks). Mitigations: 

- Reject inputs containing combining sequences larger than 128 codepoints.
- Enforce a max normalized length that maps to a safe token upper bound; if an input expands under normalization by >2x, reject with 413.

Operational Runbook (high level)

1. On tokenization-drift-high alert: open incident, capture sample of raw_inputs and normalized_preview, run token-diff tool (scripts/token_compare.sh) and assess customer impact.
2. If customer-impacting, engage product & CS to coordinate mitigation (temporary per-customer canonicalizer pinning).
3. Post-incident: capture root cause, add test to compatibility suite, and file ADR if the fix changes default behavior.

Examples

- CLI to run local compat test suite against a candidate canonicalizer: 

  ./tools/normalize_compat_test --manifest candidate_manifest.json --bucket prompt-set-serving-normalization --output report.json

- Sample canonicalizer config (YAML):

  canonicalizer:
    version: v1
    unicode: NFC
    trim_whitespace: true
    collapse_zero_width: true
    passthrough_mode_for_routes: ["embeddings_binary", "file_uploads"]

Ownership and Governance

- Owner: Model Serving Standards group (eng-serving-runtime). Primary contact: Aisha Patel.
- Review cadence: quarterly review of canonicalizer behavior and annual review before large model-family imports.
- ADR requirement: any change that affects token-count distribution by >0.5% for production traffic requires an ADR filed under architecture-and-standards/decision-records with measurable compatibility results.

Appendix: Example token-diff output (text)

- input_id: 2026-02-01-abc123
- raw_input: "Hello\u00A0World"
- normalized: "Hello World"
- tokens_before: [34, 102, 11]
- tokens_after: [34, 102, 11]
- token_delta: 0

References and related pages

- See model manifest tokenization matrix for each variant.
- Related: prompt-suite-ci-contract-testing-guidelines (for test corpus composition).
